steps.title: Lines and angles — rules to know
steps.intro: Most geometry questions are built on these rules. Know them cold.

head: Rule
Value
Remember
rows: four angles at a crossing add to \(360°\)
half of a full circle — a straight line
only if marked with a small square, or given
next to an acute angle sits an obtuse one
Adjacent angles on a straight line
they complete the same angle to \(180°\)
the two angles in its corners are equal
the two angles inside it add to \(180°\)
\(\perp\) to the same line, or \(\parallel\) to the same line
or equal small angles / small + large \(=180°\)
parallel only if given or proved
angles pointing left \(=\) angles pointing right
equal parts: count the gaps, not the points

tips: Letters instead of numbers? Plug in round numbers that look like the figure. Check that the four answers come out different — if two tie, plug in again.
Overlapping angles: add them and subtract the full turn (\(360°\)) or the straight angle (\(180°\)).
A bent line between parallels? Draw a line through each bend, parallel to both. It always works.
Adding angles to \(180°\)? Use the units digit: \(83°+54°+x=180°\) → \(3+4=7\). Therefore, \(x\) ends in \(3\).
Two lines look parallel, but nothing says so? Look for a rule that proves it: two angles inside a U that add up to \(180°\), equal small angles, or two lines \(\perp\) to the same line.

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, \(a\parallel b\). The marked lines are perpendicular. What is the value of \(x\)?
explanation: \(a\parallel b\), and small angles are equal. At line \(b\), the angle between the transversal and line \(b\) (above \(b\)) is also \(68°\).
The marked right angle is made of this \(68°\) angle and \(x\): \(68°+x=90°\).
Therefore, \(x=90°-68°=22°\). Choice 3.

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, lines \(a\) and \(b\) are both perpendicular to line \(c\). Line \(d\) crosses lines \(a\) and \(b\). What is the value of \(x\)?
choices: It cannot be determined from the information given.
explanation: \(a\perp c\) and \(b\perp c\). Two lines perpendicular to the same line are parallel. Therefore, \(a\parallel b\).
Now \(d\) is a transversal of two parallel lines. The \(50°\) angle is a small angle, and \(x\) is a large angle.
Choice 4 is the trap: "\(a\parallel b\)" is not written, but the two right angles prove it.

steps.stem:
Points \(A\), \(B\), \(C\) and \(D\) lie on a line in this order, as shown in the accompanying figure.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} AC=11 \\ BD=14 \\ AD=20 \end{cases}\)
What is the length of \(BC\)?
explanation: \(AC\) and \(BD\) overlap on \(BC\): \(AC+BD=AD+BC\).
\(11+14=20+BC\). Therefore, \(25=20+BC\) and \(BC=5\). Choice 3.
Step by step: \(AB=AD-BD=20-14=6\), and \(BC=AC-AB=11-6=5\).

steps.stem: Two parallel lines are \(7\) cm apart. A line segment joining them is perpendicular to both. What is the length of the segment (in cm)?
explanation: The distance between parallel lines is measured along a line perpendicular to both.
This segment is exactly that distance: \(7\) cm.

steps.stem: Three adjacent angles form a straight angle. Their measures are in the ratio \(2:3:4\). What is the measure of the largest angle?
explanation: \(2+3+4=9\) units make \(180°\). Therefore, one unit is \(\frac{180°}{9}=20°\).
The largest angle is \(4\) units: \(4\cdot20°=80°\).

steps.stem: A ray bisects the angle adjacent to the marked \(124°\) angle. Based on this information and the information in the accompanying figure, what is the value of \(x\)?
explanation: The angle next to \(124°\) on the straight line is \(180°-124°=56°\).
The ray cuts it into two equal halves: \(x=\frac{56°}{2}=28°\).

steps.stem: Three distinct parallel lines are intersected by a fourth line that is not parallel to them. How many distinct points of intersection are formed?
explanation: The fourth line crosses each of the three parallel lines exactly once.
The parallel lines never meet, so the three crossing points are different: \(3\) points.

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, \(a\parallel b\) and \(c\parallel d\). What is the value of \(x\)?
explanation: \(a\parallel b\) (line \(c\) crosses them): the acute angles are equal. Therefore, the acute angle next to \(x\) at the lower left is \(83°\).
\(c\parallel d\) (the diagonal crosses them): the other acute angle next to \(x\) is \(54°\).
The three angles make a straight angle: \(83°+54°+x=180°\). Therefore, \(x=180°-137°=43°\). Choice 2.
Shortcut: \(3+4=7\). Therefore, \(x\) must end in \(3\). Only \(43°\) does.

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, four lines intersect at one point. Which expression equals \(\theta\)?
explanation: The angle next to \(p\) is \(180°-p\), the angle next to \(q\) is \(180°-q\), the angle next to \(r\) is \(180°-r\).
These three angles and \(\theta\) make a straight angle: \((180°-p)+(180°-q)+(180°-r)+\theta=180°\).
Therefore, \(540°-(p+q+r)+\theta=180°\) and \(\theta=p+q+r-360°\). Choice 3.
Plug in: \(p=q=r=150°\) gives \(\theta=3\cdot30°=90°\). Choices 1, 2 and 4 give \(150°\), \(270°\) and \(-150°\). Only choice 3 gives \(90°\).

steps.title: Summary: Harder Line and Angle Questions

steps.stem: Two lines intersect. The difference between an obtuse angle and an acute angle at the intersection is \(46°\). What is the obtuse angle?
explanation:
The obtuse and the acute angle are adjacent on a straight line:
\(\begin{cases} \text{obtuse}+\text{acute}=180° \\ \text{obtuse}-\text{acute}=46° \end{cases}\)
Add the two equations: \(2\cdot\text{obtuse}=226°\). Therefore, the obtuse angle is \(113°\).

steps.stem: Two adjacent angles form a straight angle. Their bisectors are drawn from the common vertex. What is the angle between the bisectors?
explanation: Call the two angles \(2a\) and \(2b\): \(2a+2b=180°\).
The angle between the bisectors is \(a+b=\frac{180°}{2}=90°\).

steps.stem: A straight angle is divided into three parts. The second part is \(18°\) larger than the first, and the third is twice the first. What is the third angle?
explanation: Let the first angle be \(t\). The parts are \(t\), \(t+18°\) and \(2t\).
The third angle is \(2t=81°\).

steps.stem: Four rays divide a full turn into four angles. Three angles are equal, and the fourth is \(24°\) larger than each of them. What is the largest angle?
explanation: Let each of the three equal angles be \(t\). Then \(3t+(t+24°)=360°\).
\(4t=336°\). Therefore, \(t=84°\). The largest angle is \(84°+24°=108°\).

steps.stem: Based on the information in the accompanying figure, what is the value of \(x\)?
explanation: The four angles make a full circle: \(x+2x+3x+168°=360°\).

explanation: An acute angle and an obtuse angle here are small \(+\) large: \((2x+11)+(5x+1)=180\).

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, \(a\parallel b\). What is the value of \(\frac{4\alpha+\gamma}{\beta}\)?
explanation: \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are vertical angles, and \(\beta\) and \(\gamma\) are both small angles: \(\alpha=\beta=\gamma\).
\(\frac{4\alpha+\gamma}{\beta}=\frac{4\beta+\beta}{\beta}=\frac{5\beta}{\beta}=5\).

steps.stem: Five distinct lines lie in a plane. Three are parallel to one another. The other two are parallel to one another but not to the first three. How many points of intersection are formed?
explanation: Lines in the same family are parallel and never meet.
Each of the \(2\) lines meets each of the \(3\) lines once: \(2\cdot3=6\) points.

steps.stem:
Four different lines are given:
\(\begin{cases} k\perp l \\ l\perp m \\ m\perp n \end{cases}\)
Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: \(k\) and \(m\) are both perpendicular to \(l\). Two lines perpendicular to the same line are parallel: \(k\parallel m\).
(Also \(l\parallel n\), since both are perpendicular to \(m\). Therefore, choice 3, \(l\perp n\), is false.)

steps.stem:
Five different lines are given:
\(\begin{cases} p\parallel q \\ q\perp r \\ r\parallel s \\ s\perp t \end{cases}\)
Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: \(p\parallel q\) and \(q\perp r\). Therefore, \(p\perp r\). \(r\parallel s\). Therefore, \(p\perp s\) too.
\(p\perp s\) and \(t\perp s\): two lines perpendicular to the same line are parallel. Therefore, \(p\parallel t\).

steps.stem: Ten points are marked on a line, in order, at equal distances. The distance between the first point and the last point is \(45\) cm. What is the distance between the third point and the seventh point (in cm)?
explanation: Ten points make \(9\) gaps (count the gaps, not the points): each gap is \(\frac{45}{9}=5\) cm.
From the 3rd point to the 7th point there are \(7-3=4\) gaps: \(4\cdot5=20\) cm.

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, the line is divided into equal segments. What is the value of \(\frac{x}{y}\)?
explanation: \(x\) covers \(8\) equal gaps and \(y\) covers \(4\). Count the gaps, not the tick marks.

steps.stem:
Points \(A\), \(B\), \(C\) and \(D\) lie on a line in this order.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} AC=17\text{ cm} \\ BD=19\text{ cm} \\ BC=6\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is the length of \(AD\) (in cm)?
explanation: \(AC+BD=AD+BC\) (the overlap \(BC\) is counted twice).

steps.stem:
Points \(P\), \(Q\), \(R\) and \(S\) lie on a line in this order.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} a=PR \\ b=QS \end{cases}\)
Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: It cannot be determined from the information given.
explanation: \(a+b=PR+QS=(PQ+QR)+(QR+RS)\).
\(PS+QR=(PQ+QR+RS)+QR\).
Both sums have \(PQ\) once, \(RS\) once and \(QR\) twice. They are equal: \(a+b=PS+QR\).

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} \alpha+u=180° \\ \beta+3u=180° \\ 0°<u<60° \end{cases}\)
Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: It cannot be determined from the information given.
explanation: Since \(u>0\), \(3u>u\): \(\beta\) subtracts more from the same \(180°\). Therefore, \(\beta<\alpha\).
Plug in to check: \(u=10°\) gives \(\alpha=170°\) and \(\beta=150°\).

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, three lines meet at one point. The angles \(p\) and \(q\) overlap on the angle \(x\). Which expression equals \(x\)?
explanation: \(p\) and \(q\) together cover the straight angle once, and \(x\) twice: \(p+q=180°+x\).
Therefore, \(x=p+q-180°\). Choice 2.
Plug in to check: \(p=120°\), \(q=110°\) gives \(x=50°\). Choice 1 gives \(130°\), choice 3 about \(77°\), choice 4 \(-10°\).

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, line \(t\) crosses lines \(a\) and \(b\). Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: Lines \(a\) and \(b\) meet to the right of line \(t\).
Lines \(a\) and \(b\) meet to the left of line \(t\).
It cannot be determined from the information given.
explanation: The two marked angles are on the same side of \(t\), between the lines (a U): \(107°+73°=180°\).
A small angle and a large angle that add up to \(180°\) inside the U: the lines are parallel.
Therefore, \(a\parallel b\). Choice 1.
